name: Project Blue Book

summary.text: Project Blue Book was the U.S. Air Force's program for investigating reports of unidentified flying objects, run from Wright-Patterson Air Force Base and terminated on December 17, 1969. According to the Air Force, 12,618 sightings were reported to the project, of which 701 remained 'unidentified'. The decision to end it was based on the University of Colorado's Air Force-funded 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects' (the Condon Report), which concluded that nothing from 21 years of UFO study had added to scientific knowledge. The records, together with those of the predecessor projects Sign and Grudge, are held by the National Archives on microfilm publication T1206.

facts.claim: The Air Force states that of a total of 12,618 sightings reported to Project Blue Book, 701 remained 'unidentified', and that the project, headquartered at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, was terminated on December 17, 1969.

facts.claim: The Air Force says the decision to discontinue UFO investigations was based on an evaluation of the University of Colorado report 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects', reviewed by the National Academy of Sciences, and that the conclusions at termination included that there was no evidence indicating that sightings categorized as 'unidentified' were extraterrestrial vehicles.
facts.quote: The decision to discontinue UFO investigations was based on an evaluation of a report prepared by the University of Colorado entitled, "Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects;"

facts.claim: The Condon Report's first section states: 'Our general conclusion is that nothing has come from the study of UFOs in the past 21 years that has added to scientific knowledge,' and concludes that further extensive study of UFOs probably cannot be justified in the expectation that science will be advanced thereby.

facts.claim: The National Archives holds the Air Force's UFO investigation records, covering Project Sign (1947-1949), Project Grudge (1949-1952) and Project Blue Book (1952-1969), on microfilm publication T1206 (94 rolls of 35mm film). The investigations were run by the Air Technical Intelligence Center at Wright-Patterson AFB until December 17, 1969, and names of people involved in sightings were withheld from the released records.
facts.quote: they are available on archives microfilm publication T1206 (94 rolls of 35 mm film)

openQuestions: The Seamans termination memorandum itself was not located in the National Archives catalog; the date and attribution rest on the Air Force fact sheet and the National Archives Foundation article.
Sources give the project's start as 1947 (counting Sign and Grudge) or 1952 (Blue Book proper); the 12,618 total appears to cover reports to Blue Book as the Air Force counts them.
The page's '94% firmly identified' figure and the characterization of Blue Book as a public-relations buffer are interpretations not found in the official sources.
